title: 2025 National Security Strategy
summary: The 2025 National Security Strategy places economic and industrial capacity, secure infrastructure, technology leadership, energy, supply chains, and resilience inside the definition of national power. It also sets the strategic context for later defense, resilience, cyber, AI, mineral, semiconductor, nuclear, and communications actions.
key_findings: Industrial strength, domestic production, energy, technology, and supply-chain security are treated as strategic assets.
The strategy emphasizes infrastructure that can withstand disruption and protect economic continuity.
Regional priorities, alliances, trade, and standards are linked to economic and technological advantage.
why_it_matters: It is the umbrella strategy that explains why physical infrastructure and industrial policy recur across the rest of the collection.
ftfn_relevance: Supports treating industrial capacity and resilience as human-system and infrastructure variables.
Provides strategic context without substituting for agency-level execution evidence.
evidence_limits: A national strategy states priorities and worldview; it is not an implementation plan.
Political framing should be separated from later budget, regulatory, procurement, and outcome evidence.
